summary: CBS Sports' Josh Edwards presents a 2024 NFL mock draft (published November 2023) covering Round 1 picks 1 through 31, with each pick's school, size, projected team and a short rationale. Four quarterbacks go in the first round (Caleb Williams, Drake Maye, J.J. McCarthy, Jayden Daniels), while New England takes receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. at No. 3. Offensive tackles and edge rushers go heavily in the first 20 picks, and the Bengals' pick is Keon Coleman at No. 18.
one_line: Josh Edwards' November 2023 CBS Sports first-round mock draft has Caleb Williams going first, four QBs in Round 1, and Patriots taking WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
key_facts: In the mock draft, Chicago takes USC quarterback Caleb Williams at No. 1, with the piece questioning whether Justin Fields' return is too little, too late.
The N.Y. Giants take North Carolina QB Drake Maye at No. 2 because of concerns about Daniel Jones' long-term viability after his ACL injury.
New England selects Ohio State WR Marvin Harrison Jr. at No. 3, described as arguably the best talent available, though he would be catching passes from Mac Jones or Bailey Zappe.
Arizona takes Penn State OT Olumuyiwa Fashanu at No. 4, with Jonathan Gannon and Monti Ossenfort potentially moving on from D.J. Humphries.
Chicago also holds pick No. 5 and takes Alabama EDGE Dallas Turner to pair with Montez Sweat, since Yannick Ngakoue has given them nothing.
Green Bay takes Notre Dame OT Joe Alt at No. 6 as a replacement path after David Bakhtiari; L.A. Rams take Alabama OT JC Latham at No. 7.
Tennessee takes Georgia TE Brock Bowers at No. 8 to give Will Levis skill-position help; Atlanta takes Florida State EDGE Jared Verse at No. 9.
Tampa Bay takes Michigan QB J.J. McCarthy at No. 11 to replace Baker Mayfield, who was succeeded by a Michigan QB last time the Buccaneers won a title.
LSU QB Jayden Daniels goes to Minnesota at No. 21, listed with a prospect rank of 76th, because Kirk Cousins will be a free agent after the season.
Cincinnati, projected to part ways with Tee Higgins, takes Florida State WR Keon Coleman at No. 18, described as a big-bodied receiver who can win jump balls.
Iowa CB Cooper DeJean goes to Buffalo at No. 17 after it was learned his season, and potentially his Iowa career, was over.
Arizona has a second first-round pick at No. 20 (from Houston), taking Penn State EDGE Chop Robinson; Houston takes Washington EDGE Bralen Trice at No. 24 (from Cleveland).
Jacksonville takes Washington WR Rome Odunze at No. 27 to pair with Calvin Ridley; Kansas City closes the list at No. 31 with Michigan DL Kris Jenkins.
